response.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT d.A3 AS region, CASE WHEN tr.type = 'PRIJEM' THEN tr.amount WHEN tr.type = 'VYDAJ' THEN -tr.amount END AS signed_amount FROM trans tr JOIN account a ON a.account_id = tr.account_id JOIN district d ON d.district_id = a.district_id WHERE CAST(tr.date AS TEXT) BETWEEN '1996-05-09' AND '1998-01-06'), regional AS (SELECT region, AVG(signed_amount) AS avg_signed, COUNT(*) AS trans_count FROM t GROUP BY region) SELECT region, avg_signed, trans_count, avg_signed / (SELECT AVG(avg_signed) FROM regional) AS ratio FROM regional WHERE (SELECT AVG(avg_signed) FROM regional) IS NOT NULL;

assumptions.assumption: trans.date is stored as ISO text 'YYYY-MM-DD', so the text BETWEEN comparison matches the calendar range; the documentation gives YYMMDD only for account and card dates.
Both bounds are inclusive (BETWEEN), so transactions dated 1996-05-09 and 1998-01-06 are counted.
AVG ignores NULLs, so transactions of other or missing types drop out of the signed average but still count in trans_count. A region with no PRIJEM or VYDAJ rows gets a NULL average and a NULL ratio.

The overall average is an unweighted AVG over the regional averages, excluding NULL regional averages. The query does not guard against an overall average of exactly zero; SQLite then returns NULL for that ratio, while other engines may raise a division-by-zero error.
